betrayal.work: Fairy Tales From Far and Near
betrayal.author: Katherine Pyle
betrayal.locator: Pyle retelling · The Princes And The Friendly Animals; Pyle retelling · The Princes And The Friendly Animals, normalized characters 15869-17001
betrayal.excerpt: But after they had driven on and left the Prince lying there, the faithful animals did not desert him. They stayed beside him and mourned over him, and the lion licked his face and hands, but it could not revive him. Then the fox, which was very clever, reminded the animals of the flasks of ointment and healing water in the robbers’ house. The hare, which was very swift, said it would go and fetch the flasks, and it sped away to get them. Now the stepsister had wept the bowl full of tears of repentance and was free again; and when the hare came to the door and told her what it wanted, she gladly gave it the flasks and hung them about its neck in a little wicker basket. Then the hare fled back again to where the animals were waiting beside the Prince. With its tusks the boar broke the flask that held the ointment, and the bear rubbed it on the Prince’s wounds so that they were healed. Then they poured some drops from the second bottle between his lips, and the color came back to his cheeks and the light to his eyes. When they gave him to drink from the third bottle, he became quite well again and stronger than ever.
betrayal.note: Verbatim text from Katherine Pyle's 1922 English children's retelling. The collection labels it Lithuanian but does not identify an oral informant or underlying source text.

narrativeBlocks.title: The prince is betrayed
narrativeBlocks.body: On the way to the palace, two nobles kill the prince and threaten the princess into silence so one of them can claim the reward.

narrativeBlocks.title: Medicine brings him back
narrativeBlocks.body: The animals mourn beside the prince. The fox remembers healing supplies at the robbers' house; the hare fetches them, and the bear treats the wounds.

narrativeBlocks.title: A tale's sequence, not historical testimony
narrativeBlocks.body: This is one written Lithuanian-labeled story in Pyle's children's collection. Its healing water and animal helpers support claims about this plot only.

narrativeBlocks.title: A promise is finally fulfilled
narrativeBlocks.body: The rescued prince can continue to the palace, where the story's earlier rescue and betrayal are brought to light.
